name: Solomon
description: King living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David comforted Bathsheba his wife, went in unto her, and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon; and the Most High loved him, and sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, who called his name Jedidiah, because of the Most High.

Through David's judgment, Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David's lineage; David was still loved and still forgiven, which shows repentance, and that even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: David repeats the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel, that Solomon his son shall reign after him and sit upon his throne in his stead. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: David commands that Solomon be set on the king's own mule and brought to Gihon, where Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. The people come up rejoicing so that the earth rings with the sound.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: David charged Solomon his son: be thou strong, and shew thyself a man. That is what we all got to realize in these last days; we see things coming to pass. We cannot be sidetracked or pulled away with addiction and alcoholism. Now is the time to show forth the wisdom you learned.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

points: Solomon thrusts out Abiathar from being priest unto the Lord, fulfilling the word the Most High spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh. The old judgment on Eli's line is carried out.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: Shimei is commanded to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, never crossing the brook Kidron on pain of death, and he agrees. After three years he goes to Gath after his runaway servants and breaks the oath, so Solomon has Benaiah put him to death, and the kingdom is established in Solomon's hand.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: Solomon makes affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and takes his daughter, while building his own house, the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem. He loves the Lord and walks in the statutes of David his father, though the people still sacrifice in high places because no house was yet built to the name of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Kings 3: Solomon Asks for Wisdom to Judge

points: Solomon is king over all Israel, and these are the princes he set: priests, scribes, a recorder, one over the host, one over the officers, one over the household, and one over the tribute. Twelve officers provide victuals for the king and his household, each man his month in the year.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

points: And Solomon reigned over all kingdoms from the river unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt: they brought presents, and served Solomon all the days of his life. Solomon reigned over all kingdoms. So this was Israelite supremacy. That is how we are going to be again on the earth.

note.label: White Supremacy & Racism

points: And Solomon's provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal.

note.label: White Supremacy & Racism

points: And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

note.label: White Supremacy & Racism

points: Judah and Israel are as many as the sand by the sea, eating, drinking, and making merry, and Solomon reigns over all the kingdoms from the river to the border of Egypt, who bring presents and serve him. Every man dwells safely under his vine and fig tree from Dan to Beersheba.
Israel dwells safely because of the wars of King David, who put down all the surrounding nations and put them to tribute. That is why Solomon is able to rule in a time of peace.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

points: God gave Solomon largeness of heart as the sand on the seashore, and his wisdom excelled all the children of the east country, the Persians, the Indians and the Chinese, and all the wisdom of Egypt.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: The Most High gives Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, largeness of heart as the sand on the seashore, so that his wisdom excels all the children of the east country and all the wisdom of Egypt. He is wiser than all men, speaks three thousand proverbs, and his songs are a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

points: Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants to Solomon because he had heard that Solomon was anointed king in the room of his father. Hiram was ever a lover of David, so the friendship carries over to the son.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

points: When Hiram hears the words of Solomon he rejoices greatly and blesses the Lord who has given David a wise son over this great people. He agrees to supply timber of cedar and fir according to all Solomon's desire.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

points: Hiram gives Solomon cedar and fir according to all his desire, and Solomon gives Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat for food to his household and twenty measures of pure oil, year by year. The Most High gives Solomon wisdom as he promised, and there is peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they two make a league together.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

points: This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon was able to say deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built. It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

points: Solomon had order in the work, with bearers of burdens, hewers in the mountains, and above them the chief of his officers, thirty-three hundred who ruled over the people that wrought. The temple was built successfully because our forefathers had a spirit to work together under rank and structure without murmuring over who did which task.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

points: In the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, in the month Zif, he begins to build the house of the Lord. That span reaches back through the time of the judges and the reign of Saul and David, a long stretch in which Israel had no settled kingly rule until this point.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: He overlays the whole house within with gold until all is finished, the altar of cedar also covered, with a partition of gold chains before the oracle. The inside was pure gold everywhere, fit for the King, though Solomon himself confessed that the heaven of heavens cannot contain the Most High, yet this is what was made for him to dwell in while on the earth.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: Solomon's throne sat back off a porch of judgment, an area before which men would stand while the throne rose behind and above them under its own covering. He also makes a house for Pharaoh's daughter whom he had taken to wife, a marriage made, as marriages were in that time, for political gain and standing among the nations.

note.label: 1 Kings 7: Solomon's House and the Brass Work of the Temple

points: King Solomon sends and fetches Hiram out of Tyre, a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, whose father was a man of Tyre and a worker in brass. He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass.

note.label: 1 Kings 7: Solomon's House and the Brass Work of the Temple

points: Hiram makes the lavers, shovels, and basins, and finishes all the work he made for Solomon for the house of the Lord: the two pillars, the two bowls of the chapters, the two networks, four hundred pomegranates, the ten bases and their lavers, the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it. All these vessels are of bright brass, cast in the plain of Jordan in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan, left unweighed because they were exceeding many.

note.label: 1 Kings 7: Solomon's House and the Brass Work of the Temple

points: Solomon makes all the vessels of the house of the Lord: the altar of gold, the table of gold for the showbread, the candlesticks of pure gold, five on each side, with the flowers, lamps, tongs, bowls, snuffers, basins, spoons, and censers of pure gold, and the hinges of gold for the doors. When the work is ended, Solomon brings in the things David his father had dedicated, the silver, gold, and vessels, and puts them among the treasures of the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Kings 7: Solomon's House and the Brass Work of the Temple

points: Solomon assembles the elders of Israel and the heads of the tribes to bring up the ark of the covenant out of the city of David, which is Zion, in the month Ethanim, the seventh month, at the feast. This gathering is a feast of dedication for the temple, not the later feast of dedication remembered in Maccabees, but a first feasting to dedicate the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: The king and all Israel offer sacrifices before the Lord, Solomon offering a peace offering of twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep, so the king and all the people dedicate the house of the Lord. He hallows the middle of the court to offer there because the brazen altar was too little to receive the multitude of offerings.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: When Solomon had finished the building of the house of the Most High and the king's house and all he desired to do, the Most High appeared to him the second time, as he had appeared at Gibeon.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: After twenty years, when Solomon had built the two houses, Hiram king of Tyre had furnished him with cedar, fir, and gold, and Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in Galilee, but they pleased Hiram not.

Solomon gave Hiram the worst of the land, the poor cities, and Hiram was not pleased, calling them the land of Cabul to this day. Hiram had given the best cedar and fir, and in return Solomon paid him with the least, which was wisdom on Solomon's part.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: This is the reason of the levy Solomon raised to build the house of the Most High, his own house, Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer, which Pharaoh had taken and given to his daughter, Solomon's wife.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: Solomon already had the daughter of Pharaoh to wife, which was breaking a commandment, and the sin began to snowball. Yet he built cities for his chariots and horsemen and all he desired, so that he took care of his people; the Most High had given him wisdom that no man on earth had except Christ.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: Of the children of Israel Solomon made no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, princes, captains, and rulers of his chariots and horsemen; instead of enslaving his own people he built them up and gave them positions.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: Pharaoh's daughter came up to her house that Solomon built, and Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings three times a year, and burnt incense before the Most High, and so finished the house.

Ophir was famous for its gold from very early days; Solomon had the wisdom to know the routes and the times of year to sail, and no one could undermine him, for he had the power, the wisdom, the money, and the knowledge.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: King Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion-geber, beside Eloth on the shore of the Red Sea, the same port the voyagers to Brazil left from. Solomon was known in antiquity to send ships to this side of the world.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

points: Solomon made a navy of ships at Eziongeber on the shore of the Red Sea, and Hiram sent shipmen that had knowledge of the sea with Solomon's servants, and they fetched from Ophir gold, four hundred and twenty talents.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

points: When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Most High, she came to prove him with hard questions, and came to Jerusalem with a great train, camels bearing spices, much gold, and precious stones.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She communed with him of all that was in her heart, and Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hid from the king that he told her not.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great store, and precious stones; and the navy of Hiram brought from Ophir great plenty of almug trees and precious stones, of which Solomon made pillars for the house of the Most High and harps and psalteries for singers.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked. People assume this was sexual, but her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order; the word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think, as the law shows the tithe money could be spent on whatever the soul lusted after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food.

Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents, besides that of the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors. He made two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold, and a great throne of ivory overlaid with the best gold.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and wisdom, and all the earth sought him to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart, bringing presents year by year. No king reigned like Solomon or was richer than him.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: Solomon loved many strange women, and they turned his heart to other gods. He built high places for Chemosh and Molech for his Moabite and Ammonite wives.
The prophet Ahijah tore Jeroboam's garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten. God would take ten tribes from Solomon's son and leave one tribe for David's sake.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Solomon loved many strange women besides the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites, nations the Most High had said Israel should not join with, for surely they would turn their heart after their gods; and Solomon clave to these in love.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: King Solomon loved many strange women, of the nations concerning which the Lord said, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods. It did not say maybe; it said surely. That is why we are not supposed to be dealing with the other nations.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

points: King Solomon loved many strange women, of the nations concerning which the Lord said, ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because he is taking foreign women.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart after other gods. Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians: Ashtoreth is where Easter comes from, the goddess of fertility. Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon. That is where that star came in: the star of Remphan, the star of Molech, witchcraft. Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice.

Being that Solomon was into it, the navy was involved in it; that is the reason you see those symbols in some of the records of the people that came over. But that is not a symbol we are supposed to be dealing with. It is not the Star of David; that is not in the Bible.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

points: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and built high places for Chemosh and for Molech, and did likewise for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: When Solomon was old his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Most High as David his father's was; he went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and did evil in the sight of the Most High.
David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin; this is why a righteous man falls seven times and rises again.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: He said, I will raise up the tabernacle of David that has fallen. What happened? Solomon got old; he has 700 wives and 300 concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They all did not serve the same god: you had Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of these gods required child sacrifice; some of these gods involved sexual orgies. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. And you had to pay taxes for those gods.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: The Most High was angry with Solomon because his heart was turned from him who had appeared to him twice and commanded him not to go after other gods, but he kept not the commandment.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Therefore the Most High said he would surely rend the kingdom from Solomon and give it to his servant, but not in Solomon's days for David's sake; he would rend it out of the hand of his son.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The Most High also stirred up Rezin the son of Eliadah, who gathered men, reigned in Damascus, and was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon. There was peace under Solomon while he kept the commandments, but when he broke them the Most High gave strength to his enemies.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant, a mighty man of valor, lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon had made him ruler over the charge of the house of Joseph, which was the two tribes Ephraim and Manasseh.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon and his wisdom are written in the book of the acts of Solomon; he reigned in Jerusalem over Israel forty years, then slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Rehoboam consulted with the old men that stood before Solomon his father: how do ye advise that I may answer this people? But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him: those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men, how do you advise that I may answer this people; to the young men, what counsel give ye that we may answer this people? Meaning we all together, y'all my peers, we running this thing.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with.

Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Rehoboam replaces the gold shields with brass, marking Israel's fall from gold to brass, from the riches of Solomon's day to loss.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: He defiled the high places Solomon had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, the abominations of the Zidonians, Moabites, and Ammonites, and broke in pieces the images, cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: Nebuchadnezzar carried out all the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and cut in pieces the vessels of gold Solomon had made, as the Lord had said.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: The sons born to David in Jerusalem are named, including Solomon, born of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: The kings of Judah are set down in order from Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on through the line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: This is a good and honorable lineage, the men who executed the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: David carried the gold and much brass back to Jerusalem, the brass out of which Solomon would later make the brazen sea, the pillars, and the vessels.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 18: The Victories of King David

points: David said that Solomon his son was young and tender, and the house to be built for the Lord must be exceeding magnifical, of fame and glory throughout all countries, so he prepared abundantly before his death.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: He called for Solomon his son and charged him to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: The Lord promised David a son who would be a man of rest, to whom he would give rest from all his enemies round about, whose name would be Solomon, and in whose days he would give peace and quietness unto Israel. This son would build the house for the Most High's name, and the Most High would establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: When David was old and full of days, he made Solomon his son king over Israel and gathered together all the princes of Israel with the priests and the Levites. The Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and upward, and their number man by man was thirty and eight thousand.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 23: The Numbering and Ordering of the Levites

points: I will establish his kingdom forever: Solomon's kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren's; no one outside Solomon's loins can sit on that throne, so if Christ is not of the Solomonic line he is not entitled to it.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him exceedingly. The Most High established Solomon before he ever built the house.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

points: Solomon spake to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to every governor, the chief of the fathers, and went with all the congregation to the high place at Gibeon, where the tabernacle of the congregation that Moses had made in the wilderness was.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

points: The brasen altar that Bezaleel the son of Uri had made was set before the tabernacle of the Lord, and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it. Solomon went up to that brasen altar before the Lord and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

points: In that night the Most High appeared unto Solomon and said, Ask what I shall give thee. This same account is told in First Kings chapter 3, where the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; reading it there gives more detail of what was said.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

points: The Most High said to Solomon that because this was in his heart, and he had not asked riches, wealth, honor, the life of his enemies, nor long life, but wisdom and knowledge to judge the people, wisdom and knowledge were granted unto him.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

points: Solomon returned from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel. He gathered chariots and horsemen, having a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

points: Solomon determined to build a house for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom. Where did Solomon get this understanding and this vision. It came from his father David, who charged him to build the house.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

points: Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them. This is the same labor force spoken of again at the end of the chapter.

David had told Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, warning that if he sought Him he would be found, but if he forsook Him he would be cast off. David then gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

points: Solomon numbered all the strangers in the land of Israel, after the numbering David his father had made, and they were found a hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred.

David had prepared for the house long before, telling Solomon that in his trouble he had laid up a hundred thousand talents of gold, a thousand thousand talents of silver, brass and iron without weight, timber and stone, and workmen in abundance. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

points: Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father, in the place David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. This threshingfloor was read of a few days ago in First Chronicles 21.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 3: Solomon Builds the Temple

points: Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basons, and finished the work he was to make for king Solomon for the house of God: the two pillars, the pommels and the chapiters on the top of the two pillars, and the two wreaths to cover the two pommels of the chapiters upon the pillars.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made one sea and twelve oxen under it, the pots, the shovels, the fleshhooks, and all their instruments, which Huram his father made for king Solomon for the house of the Lord, of bright brass.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: In the plain of Jordan the king cast them in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah. Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance, for the weight of the brass could not be found out.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: Solomon made all the vessels that were for the house of God: the golden altar, and the tables whereon the shewbread was set.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: The work of the house of the Most High was finished, and Solomon brought in all that David his father had dedicated, the silver, the gold, and the instruments, and laid them among the treasures of the house.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, and the chiefs of the fathers to bring up the ark of the covenant out of the city of David, which is Zion.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: Solomon and all the congregation before the ark sacrificed sheep and oxen that could not be numbered for multitude. This was a celebration, a gathered nation of Israel in order, in beautiful garments, keeping the appointed feast together.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: Solomon declared that the Most High had said He would dwell in the thick darkness, and that Solomon had built Him a house of habitation, a place for His dwelling for ever.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 6: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication

points: Solomon stood before the altar in the presence of all the congregation and spread forth his hands, having made a brazen scaffold five cubits long, five broad, and three high, on which he kneeled before all Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 6: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication

points: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Most High filled the house so the priests could not enter.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

points: The king and all the people offered sacrifice, Solomon offering twenty and two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep, and so dedicated the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

points: Solomon hallowed the middle of the court for offerings because the brazen altar could not receive them all, kept the feast seven days with all Israel from Hamath to the river of Egypt, and on the eighth day held a solemn assembly.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

points: They kept the dedication of the altar seven days and the feast seven days. On the twenty-third day of the seventh month the people went home glad and merry in heart for the goodness the Most High had shown to David, Solomon, and Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

points: Solomon finished the house of the Most High and his own house, and all that came into his heart to make he prosperously effected, and the Most High appeared to him by night.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

points: The Most High told Solomon He had heard his prayer and chosen this place for a house of sacrifice. To be told the prayer was heard is itself an honor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

points: At the end of twenty years in which Solomon built the house of the Most High and his own house, he built the cities Hiram had restored to him and caused the children of Israel to dwell there.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: Israel was royalty, building whole cities across the land of Solomon's dominion, in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and wherever he desired to build.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: These nations were sons of Canaan, not Israel, and their descendants left in the land paid tribute, that is taxes, to Israel. The kingdom was so strong that other nations paid Israel, and Solomon had two hundred and fifty officers ruling over the people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter out of the city of David to the house he had built for her, saying his wife should not dwell in David's house because the places were holy where the ark had come.
The presence of the ark set the city of David apart as holy. Solomon would not let his wife dwell where that holiness rested.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: All the work of Solomon was prepared and finished, the house of the Most High perfected, and then Solomon went to Eziongeber and Eloth on the seaside in Edom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: Hiram sent ships and servants who had knowledge of the sea, and they went with Solomon's servants to Ophir and brought back four hundred and fifty talents of gold to king Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: The Queen of Sheba hears of the fame of Solomon in her own land and travels to Jerusalem to prove him, meaning to test him, with hard questions from what she has heard.
Solomon answers every question she brings; nothing is hidden from him that he cannot explain to her.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The queen gives Solomon 120 talents of gold, spices in great abundance, and precious stones; there was never such spice as she brought.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon gives the queen all she desires beyond what she brought, and she returns to her own land.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The weight of gold coming to Solomon in one year is six hundred sixty and six talents, beyond what merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors bring.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom, and all of them seek his presence to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon has four thousand stalls for horses and chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, stationed in the chariot cities and at Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon are written in the book of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
After all these great works Solomon dies, and the account turns to his son who is raised up next.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon reigns in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years, then sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and his son Rehoboam reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Rehoboam goes to Shechem where all Israel has gathered to make him king, and Jeroboam the son of Nebat returns out of Egypt where he had fled from Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam first takes counsel with the old men who stood before Solomon while his father lived, asking what answer to return.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Shishak takes away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, carrying off all the shields of gold Solomon had made.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: He names Jeroboam as the servant of Solomon who rose up and rebelled against his lord. To understand that rebellion, the account goes back to 1 Kings 11.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Young and tenderhearted does not mean a small child. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign; he simply knew nothing of war, for the land had rest in Solomon's days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: He set the carved image in the house where the Lord had promised David and Solomon to put his name for ever and never again move Israel out of the land, on condition that they keep the whole law by the hand of Moses.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: He sets a carved idol in the house of God, the very house of which the Most High said to David and Solomon, In this house and in Jerusalem will I put my name for ever, and Manasseh makes Judah do worse than the heathen the Lord destroyed before them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: He sets the priests in their charges, encourages them to the service of the house of the Lord, and tells the Levites to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built and to serve the Lord and his people Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: The priests, Levites, singers, porters, Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants are all counted.

note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

points: The priests, the Levites, the singers, the porters, the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants are all counted by their houses.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: Men were appointed over the chambers for the treasures, the offerings, the firstfruits, and the tithes, and both singers and porters kept the ward of their God according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son, and the portions were given every day.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel. Solomon is giving understanding in this proverb, and from the very top he is basically talking about the fear of the Most High and understanding.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: These are also proverbs of Solomon copied out by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah. Hezekiah and his men studied Solomon's writings because they understood that what was written before their time was written for our learning, to seek out the ways of our fathers and find the right paths.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

points: The book opens, "The song of songs, which is Solomon's." Solomon is the author, not a woman, though that is the doctrine some try to push. The plain words of verse one say these songs belong to Solomon.
Solomon was a poet. The Most High gave him wisdom and largeness of heart, and he spoke three thousand proverbs and his songs were a thousand and five, which shows plainly who wrote this book.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: The bride says, "I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem," likening herself to the tents of Kedar and the curtains of Solomon.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: “I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem”. Solomon is black and good-looking, black and handsome. Correlate blackness with being good-looking. God said it. To hell with what this world says. Believe and teach it. Sisters have trouble complimenting another sister, saying she looks cute. Why? Encourage each other. Brothers, don't go telling another brother he's cute or handsome like that.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

points: She points to Solomon's bed, with threescore valiant men of Israel about it, every man with his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

note.label: Song of Solomon 3: Seeking Him Whom My Soul Loveth

points: She calls the daughters of Zion to go forth and behold King Solomon with the crown his mother crowned him with in the day of his espousals, the day of the gladness of his heart.

note.label: Song of Solomon 3: Seeking Him Whom My Soul Loveth

points: Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon and let it out to keepers, every one to bring a thousand pieces of silver for the fruit, and his own vineyard is before him.
The vineyard repeated through the whole book is Israel; wherever Solomon names the vineyard, the fruit, or the garden, he is speaking of the house of Israel.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

points: David begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias, and the kings run Roboam, Abia, Asa, Josaphat, Joram, Ozias, Joatham, Achaz, Ezekias, Manasses, Amon and Josias.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and the queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. These men had a greater than both standing in front of them and would not hear.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

points: The queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and a greater than Solomon is here.

note.label: Luke 11: How to Pray, the Strong Man, and the Woes
